_readme: The organisation's own context: what is signed, who is allowed to do what,
which ranges are lab, which destinations are sanctioned.
This is TRUSTED input. Unlike everything in an alert, it is not written by
whoever triggered the alert — it comes from asset inventory, the identity
provider and change management. That is precisely why it can be used to
decide that something was authorised, and why an attacker cannot add
themselves to it by naming a process cleverly.
In a real deployment this file is generated from the CMDB, the IdP's service
account list, and the change calendar. Here it is hand-written to match the
synthetic corpus, and every claim in it is fictional.
AUTHORISATION IS SCOPED. `max_privilege` is the point of the design: knowing
an account is not the same as that account being allowed to do the specific
thing observed. svc_helpdesk is a known automation account and is still not
permitted to touch Domain Admins — an unscoped allowlist would have excused
exactly that, which is the confused-deputy failure this file is shaped to
avoid. The first scorecard run with an unscoped list produced a missed true
positive on TP-05.
Without this file Bishop still runs — it simply cannot distinguish
'authorised' from 'malicious', so an approved red-team exercise reads as a
genuine intrusion. That is the correct failure direction.

svc_intune.note: Endpoint management. Provisions workstations and sets local group membership during onboarding.

svc_veeam.note: Backup service. Archives file shares to the backup volume nightly.

svc_build.note: Build agent. Fetches toolchains from the internal artefact server.

svc_helpdesk.note: Helpdesk automation. Resets passwords and unlocks accounts. NOT permitted to change domain group membership.

system.note: Local system, used by management agents.

p.almeida-adm.note: Platform team. Authorised for scheduled maintenance on application servers.

authorised_test_ranges.note: Red team range. Offensive tooling here is expected and covered by a standing rules-of-engagement document.

scanner_sources.10.20.5.99: Authenticated vulnerability scanner. Weekly credentialed sweep; failed logins against test accounts are expected and the rule should exclude this source.

sanctioned_destinations.intake.monitoring.example: Monitoring vendor intake endpoint. Agents check in on a fixed interval by design.
